# AI log – Task 1

**Tool:** Claude Code (VS Code, WSL) with the model Claude Opus 5.5, used throughout; the app itself was generated by a Claude Code sub-agent with the same model. **Inputs the AI worked with:** the Part A spec plus a short process wrapper as the generation prompt (`generation-prompt.md`); the `CLAUDE.md` files (course rules, working rules), loaded automatically in every session; `guidelines.md` (pinned best practices with sources, also the review checklist).

| Tool, model | What for? | Key prompts (summary) | Adopted, changed or discarded? | AI errors and own corrections |
|----|------|------------|-------|-------------|
| Claude Code, Opus 5.5 | Part A: task, spec, working rules, guidelines | Explain the task PDF; Kotlin best practices; "what do we want to achieve with the app?"; one decision at a time; spec down to one page | Spec text drafted by the AI, every decision made by the student; guidelines adopted | Unrealistic fall scenario as the reason for the notification → challenged, warning renamed to "Strong shock detected" (5); five decisions at once → rule: one at a time (3) |
| Claude Code, Opus 5.5 | Part B: project skeleton | Git before the skeleton; app ID without the student's name | Adopted; API level changed | Compiled against API 36, build failed → API 37 (2); no app icon → added (13, F5) |
| Claude Code sub-agent, Opus 5.5 | Part B: generate the app | Spec as the prompt, plus: work alone, build until it succeeds, list every assumption; guidelines as coding rules | Adopted unchanged as a raw commit, then five review fixes, one commit each | Notification tap opened a second screen with fresh data → launcher intent (F4); missing sensor not logged → log line (F3) |
| Claude Code, Opus 5.5 | Part C: review support, emulator checks | One checklist item at a time; extend the frozen spec with amendments instead of editing it | Verdicts and findings checked by the student | Test commands stacked copies of the app's screen and ran steps from the wrong state → launch like the launcher, clean state per step (11, 12) |
| Claude Code, Opus 5.5 | Part D: measurement script, evaluation | Inject ideal values, 5 runs each; keep the GPS step sizes in the report; read the whole PDF to keep the scope right | Script and report adopted after fixes | First GPS step too fast, 2 of 5 runs wrong → script fixed, series repeated (15); wrong explanation of the GPS step sizes → dropped (16) |
| Claude Code, Opus 5.5 | Part E, documentation | "what does the task description say?"; decide edge vs. cloud | Recommendation decided by the student (device; cloud only for training) | Proposed research the task doesn't ask for → dropped (17) |

Numbers in brackets refer to `ai-errors.md`, F1–F5 to `review.md`.

**Where did the AI save time?** Generating the app from the one-page spec took 22 minutes: 16 Kotlin files, about 1,700 lines, and the first build succeeded without warnings (`generation-prompt.md`, `generation-report.md`). The AI drove the emulator over `adb` (permission dialogs, lifecycle, a removed sensor, injected values), so every check was repeatable and left log excerpts as evidence (`review.md`). One script it wrote ran all Part D experiments, 5 runs each, unattended in about 20 minutes (CSV times 16:22–16:40). It also found and quoted sources quickly (Android docs and source code, GDPR).

**Where did it make errors, and how were they noticed?** `ai-errors.md` lists 17: 9 in tooling, 3 in the way of working, 3 in reasoning, 1 in the build and 1 in code; the review found two more in the code (F3, F4). Code and build errors were found by checks, not by reading the AI's own report: the failing build, Android Lint and tests on the emulator. Tooling errors showed in the command output: timeouts, unreadable screenshots, implausible results (100.3 m instead of 111.2 m in two GPS runs). Errors in the way of working and in reasoning were caught by the student, who challenged a weak argument, the way decisions were presented and work beyond the task; each of the three about the way of working became a rule in `CLAUDE.md`. The AI found one reasoning error itself by checking a hypothesis against the data (16). F1 and F2 were gaps in our own spec, not AI errors (no plausibility limit for GPS steps; a library list that contradicted the required APIs); both were fixed by spec amendments.
